 ORDER Learned High Court Government Pleader accepts notice for respondent No.1.
2.

The present writ petition is filed by one Hanumappa son of Rudrappa Hoddannavar who is accused in SC/ST.No.4/2022 against the order dated 27.07.2023 on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag, wherein, the application filed by the Public Prosecutor under Section 216 of Cr.P.C., to frame additional charge for the offences punishable under section 376 of IPC against the accused was allowed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State.
4.
Brief facts of the case are that respondent No.2 filed a complaint against the petitioner before the Gajendragad police on 10.01.2022.

On the basis of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:12479 said complaint, the concerned police had registered a case in Crime No.4/2022 for the offences punishable under sections 323, 405 and 506 of IPC and under Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(va) of SC/ST PA Act 1989 Amended Act 2005 and after investigation they filed charge sheet against the petitioner/accused before the Trial Court.
5.

The evidence of the prosecution witnesses had commenced and respondent No.2/complainant has examined as PW.1 and after completion of her examination-in-chief, the public prosecutor filed application under section 216 of Cr.P.C. to frame a charge against the accused/petitioner for the offence under section 376 of IPC by altering charge.
6. The petitioner herein filed objections to the said application.
The trial court by considering the application and the objections filed, has allowed the application.
Aggrieved by which, the petitioner is before this Court.
This Court has carefully considered the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel on both sides and perused the material on record.

sentences.text: The material on record reveals that the application was filed under section 216 of Cr.P.C. Section 216 of Cr.P.C. states that, the Court at any stage before pronouncement of the judgment can alter or to add any charge at any time.

In light of the said circumstances, the learned judge has allowed the application and also held that the accused side will be given an opportunity for cross-examination of the prosecution side witnesses to establish the defence on additional charge.

The Court was of the considered opinion that the framing of additional charge for the offence under section 376 of IPC would not put the accused under surprise for the reason that the allegations in respect of sexual harassment is mentioned on the first information itself.

The material on record as brought to the notice of this Court by learned High Court Government Pleader at page No.82 of the evidence of NC:
2023:KHC-D:12479 PW.1 at paragraph No.7, which evidences that she has stated about the sexual harassment by the accused.
In light of the said circumstances, learned judge taking into consideration all the material on record and having found that the Court can add any charge at any time has passed the impugned order.
9. On perusal of the impugned order would evidence that the same does not call for any interference by this Court.
Accordingly, this court pass the following;
ORDER The writ petition is dismissed.
The impugned order at Annexure-A stands confirmed.
